newsitem.title: USA: G7 to call for continued forex cooperation.
newsitem.headline: G7 to call for continued forex cooperation.

text.p: The Group of Seven rich nations will call for continued cooperation on macroeconomic policies and foreign exchange in a statement due for release later on Saturday, a G7 source said.
The statement would also urge France, Germany and Italy to continue the reduction of public deficits and implement structural reforms to reduce unemployment, the source said.

The Group of Seven -- the United States, Canada, Japan, Britain, France, Germany and Italy -- were expected to reiterate a call to stick to policies promoting sustainable non-inflationary growth, the source said.

They would note that the economic outlook, in terms of sound growth and low inflation, was favourable, but work remained to be done to bolster public finances, while unemployment in some of the member countries remained a worry.
The statement would note that G7 leaders had "asked our finance ministers to continue to cooperate closely on economic policy and in the exchange markets", the source said.
France, Germany and Italy must foster job creation through reducing public deficits and structural reform.
The statement would say that "...they will need to deepen structural reforms to reduce barriers to job creation."
